sections.content:
Population change in South Derbyshire in 2032

The population in South Derbyshire is projected to increase from 111,145 people in 2022 to 132,463 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 20,148 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in South Derbyshire
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In South Derbyshire, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 931, with 12,081 births and 11,150 deaths in South Derbyshire between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in South Derbyshire by 0.8%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 20,148, with 91,710 people moving to the area and 71,562 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Derbyshire by 18.1%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 676, with 1,286 people moving to the area and 1,962 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in South Derbyshire by 0.6%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 806, with 2,541 people moving to the area and 1,735 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Derbyshire by 0.7%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in South Derbyshire in 2032

The median age in South Derbyshire is projected to rise from 41 years in 2022 to 42 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 20% of the population in South Derbyshire are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 18% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in South Derbyshire between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in South Derbyshire is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 276 to 285 over the same time period.

This is around average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in South Derbyshire?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 22% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in South Derbyshire between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
